# Hand-crafted Codenames test vectors (fixture, NOT a real embedding).
#
# Standard GloVe/word2vec text format: one `word v1 v2 ... v12` line per entry.
# 12 dimensions: axes 0..7 are the eight semantic clusters, axes 8..11 carry a
# per-word residual (+/-) that separates cluster members from one another.
#
#   cluster centroid c_i        = 1.00 * e_i
#   cluster member  w_(i,j)     = 0.98 * e_i + (+/-)0.199 * e_(8 + j % 4)
#
# so the geometry is exact and every ranking below is unambiguous:
#
#   cos(c_i, w_(i,j))           = 0.98     centroid vs. its own cluster
#   cos(c_i, w_(k,j)), k != i   = 0.00     centroid vs. any other cluster
#   cos(w_(i,j), w_(i,k))       = 0.96 / 0.92   two members of one cluster
#   cos(w_(i,j), w_(k,l))       = 0.00 / +-0.04 members of different clusters
#
# A centroid is therefore always the strictly best clue for its own cluster,
# and it is the only candidate with zero leakage onto the other seven.
# The eight cluster words per cluster are all on the vendored wordlist
# (assets/codenames_words.txt); the centroids and the four distractors are
# deliberately NOT, and are legal clues against every word on it.
